chapter: First Blue Note recording with Jackie McLean
title: Meeting Jackie McLean through Jim Harrison and the Blue Coronet
summary: Jim Harrison sends Tolliver to Jackie McLean after a jam at the Blue Coronet in Brooklyn; McLean hears his tunes and books him for the next record date.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I wonder if we return to that 1964 date with Jackie if you can describe or you have a specific memory of that first recording and being in the studio or wherever it was and thinking, I’m trying to phrase this — did you have a feeling like yeah, now I’m getting there. Now I’m jumping in? This is a significant moment for me?

I’ll say this, at one point my knees were shaking you know. You know when I decided to leave Howard University with my pharmacy studies and grapple with this thing, that was the moment where I said I know I can do this. And so anything that came after that was like gravy for me because I, you know, I knew I could play that trumpet now the way I was hearing it. And so what stood out for me was that Jackie McLean, so I was sent to Jackie McLean, who actually is the guy responsible for me being where I am in terms of being in this now, Jim Harrison, God bless him he’s still alive. So he, he had a Jackie McLean fan club. And in 1963 when I came back home why he was going around and you’re doing all the jam sessions of course, and this famous place in Brooklyn called the Blue Coronet, he was there listening, happened to be there that night and you know I’m jamming on the bandstand with some new arrivals to New York nobody had heard of before either, you know Jack DeJohnette. And we’re all brand new to this stuff you know, the scene. And so he come up to the bandstand and Jim Harrison said, “Okay, by the way, you know Jackie McLean is, he might be looking for a trumpet player.” And he sent me to Jackie and that’s how I met Jackie. I told him that Jim Harrison sent me. And Jackie said, “Okay, come see me at this time” and see what’s going on. So I went to Jackie’s house and he says, “I’ve got these tunes. Let’s go over them.” He played them. © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-
